name: Podman
summary: A daemonless container and pod manager that uses OCI-compatible image, storage, networking, and runtime components and supports running workloads without root privileges.

features.name: Daemonless container control
features.description: Podman exposes a Docker-compatible CLI and manages containers, images, volumes, and pods through its libpod library without requiring a persistent manager daemon.
benefits: Reduces idle shared-daemon exposure and resource use
Provides direct CLI and library lifecycle control
costs: Client process lifetime and local state become operational concerns
Remote API use is a separate service boundary

features.name: Rootless user-namespace runtime
features.description: On Linux, rootless Podman uses user namespaces and identity mappings, normally including subordinate IDs, to run container processes within the invoking user's host permissions. The default container-root mapping and alternative user namespace modes remain constrained by those permissions.
benefits: Supports container workflows without a root manager daemon
Limits container privilege to the launching user under the documented kernel permission model
costs: Kernel, subuid/subgid, filesystem, networking, and cgroup constraints remain
Some operations and image sharing have reduced functionality; multi-ID setup can require privileged mapping helpers

features.name: OCI image and pod composition
features.description: Podman composes OCI or Docker images, containers, and pods from specialized libraries and OCI runtimes, with pods grouping containers that share selected resources.
benefits: Reuses ecosystem image and runtime contracts
Groups related containers under one lifecycle model
costs: Behavior depends on runtime, storage, networking, and build component compatibility
Shared pod resources create coordination constraints

mathematical_views.question: How does a user-level Podman invocation refine into a container process with mapped identities and host-kernel controls?
assumptions: The host kernel implements user namespaces and requested controls
Identity mappings are part of the execution state
The view does not claim complete isolation from kernel vulnerabilities

mathematical_views.question: Which image, container, pod, storage, network, and OCI-runtime nodes must compose for a workload lifecycle?
assumptions: Nodes represent managed objects or component boundaries
Edges represent ownership or required coordination
The graph abstracts implementation details of external OCI projects

costs: Lifecycle coordination is distributed across invocations and services
Kernel and filesystem limitations reduce feature parity
